name: Miami
tagline: Tropical Art Deco glamour where Latin America meets the sea.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: November to April is warm, dry and in full swing, from Art Basel in December to the March music and tennis weeks; summer is hot, humid and hurricane-prone.

ourTake.lede: Miami is two cities, the beach and the mainland, and the interesting one is increasingly the mainland: the Design District, Wynwood, and the Cuban weight of Little Havana. Use South Beach for the Art Deco architecture and a swim, but base yourself with intent rather than defaulting to the ocean-front strip. The heat and humidity are real; the season that matters runs roughly November to April.
ourTake.comeIf: You want art-deco beaches, Latin energy and a serious nightlife.
ourTake.skipIf: You want culture, quiet or a manageable flight.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Four Seasons Hotel at The Surf Club
items.description: A restored 1930s beach club turned Richard Meier landmark, the most complete luxury address on the Miami sand.

items.name: The Setai, Miami Beach
items.description: A serene Art Deco-meets-Asian sanctuary on Collins Avenue, the quietest true luxury on the beach.

items.name: Faena Hotel Miami Beach
items.description: Alan Faena's theatrical red-and-gold fantasy, a Damien Hirst gilded mammoth and a cabaret theatre on the sand.

items.name: Acqualina Resort & Residences on the Beach
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide 5-Star Hotel & Spa (2026, 14th consecutive year)
The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A Mediterranean palazzo on the Sunny Isles sand, Forbes Five-Star for hotel and spa, fourteen years running.

items.name: The St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort
items.description: The grand oceanfront St. Regis beside Bal Harbour Shops, butler service and a rarefied, moneyed calm.

items.name: 1 Hotel South Beach
items.description: A living-green, reclaimed-wood sanctuary on Collins, sustainable luxury with four pools and the beach at the door.

items.name: Nobu Hotel Miami Beach
credentials: Part of the Nobu Hospitality maison (Robert De Niro & Nobu Matsuhisa)
Home to the flagship Nobu Miami restaurant
items.description: The Nobu world made a hotel inside the Eden Roc, Japanese-minimalist rooms above the flagship restaurant.

items.name: The Miami Beach EDITION
items.description: Ian Schrager's polished, playful oceanfront tower, a skating rink and bowling alley beneath quiet-luxury rooms.

items.name: Mr. C Miami – Coconut Grove
items.description: The Cipriani family's intimate Italian-styled tower over the Grove, old-world Venetian service in leafy Miami.

items.name: The Betsy – South Beach
items.description: A colonial-white Ocean Drive landmark with a literary soul, the most cultured small hotel in South Beach.

items.name: Ocean Drive & the Art Deco Historic District
credentials: Miami Beach Architectural District, U.S. National Register of Historic Places
items.description: A mile of pastel 1920s–30s hotels in candy colours, neon and porthole windows, the largest concentration of Art Deco architecture in the world. Walk it early morning before the heat, camera in hand; the multi-gen crowd loves it and the light on the facades is best just after sunrise.

items.name: Art Deco walking tour (Miami Design Preservation League)
items.description: The definitive 90-minute guided walk from the 1001 Ocean Drive welcome centre, decoding the streamline-moderne facades, the theming, and how a preservation battle in the 1980s saved the district. A cultured, easy outing for parents and grandparents who want the story, not just the photo.

items.name: Wynwood Walls
items.description: The world's largest outdoor street-art museum, a curated open-air courtyard of monumental murals by 120-plus artists from 25-plus countries, rotated regularly. Entry is now timed and ticketed through the welcome centre, so pre-book; the surrounding streets are free to roam.

items.name: Wynwood Arts District galleries & mural streets
items.description: Beyond the Walls, the whole neighbourhood is a canvas, galleries, warehouses, breweries and cafes wrapped in ever-changing murals. Come on a Second Saturday Art Walk when studios open late; a relaxed evening for design-minded families before dinner.

items.name: Miami Design District
items.description: A walkable open-air quarter where flagship maisons, Louis Vuitton, Dior, Hermès, Cartier, Bulgari, sit among public art, Buckminster Fuller's Fly's Eye Dome and sculpture-lined plazas. Serious shopping paired with architecture and art, valet-easy and unhurried.

items.name: Institute of Contemporary Art (ICA Miami)
items.description: A sharp, free-admission contemporary-art museum with a sculpture garden, set right in the Design District so you can pair it with the boutiques. A quick, refined cultural stop that never feels like homework.

items.name: Vizcaya Museum & Gardens
items.description: James Deering's 1916 Italian-Renaissance villa on Biscayne Bay, with formal gardens, a stone barge breakwater and antique-filled rooms, the most romantic estate in Miami. A multi-generational favourite; go on a weekday morning and linger in the gardens before the tour crowds.

items.name: Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM)
items.description: Herzog & de Meuron's hanging-garden pavilion on the downtown bayfront holds 20th- and 21st-century international art, with terraces over Biscayne Bay. The cafe and shaded verandah make it easy with elders and children in tow.

items.name: Phillip & Patricia Frost Museum of Science
items.description: A planetarium, a three-level aquarium and hands-on galleries share the bayfront park with PAMM, the two sell a combo pass. The most reliable half-day for grandchildren, with plenty of air-conditioned space when the sun is fierce.

items.name: The Bass
items.description: Miami Beach's contemporary-art museum in a restored 1930s Art Deco building by Russell Pancoast, the first public exhibition space in South Florida. Compact and beautifully curated, a short walk from Collins Avenue and easy to fold into a beach day.

items.name: Rubell Museum
items.description: One of the largest private contemporary-art collections in the U.S., shown across a converted warehouse complex with a courtyard, garden and excellent restaurant. A quieter, connoisseur's alternative to the marquee museums, ideal for collectors.

items.name: Superblue Miami
items.description: An experiential-art destination built for immersive installations, mirrored infinity rooms and light works you walk through. Genuinely wondrous for children and grown-ups alike; book a timed slot and pair it with the Rubell nearby.

items.name: Little Havana & Calle Ocho
items.description: The heart of Cuban Miami, cigar rollers, fruit stands, rum bars, galleries and the aroma of cafecito along SW 8th Street. Come for the walk, the music and a guava pastry; the veg-aware will find plenty in the fruit shakes and rice-and-plantain plates.

items.name: Máximo Gómez (Domino) Park
items.description: A tiny corner park where elders have gathered over dominoes and heated debate for four decades, pure, unstaged neighbourhood life. Open daily; stand at the rail and watch, a memorable few minutes for grandparents who recognise the ritual.

items.name: Ball & Chain
items.description: A live-music landmark on Calle Ocho since 1935, with indoor and courtyard stages, salsa and no cover charge. An authentic Havana-style evening, free salsa lessons on Thursdays if the younger set wants to try.

items.name: The Biltmore Hotel
items.description: A 1926 Mediterranean-revival landmark with a soaring lobby, a Donald Ross golf course and the largest hotel pool on the U.S. East Coast, set in 150 acres. Take afternoon tea or a heritage tour even if you're not staying, grand, hushed, old-world luxury.

items.name: Venetian Pool
credentials: U.S. National Register of Historic Places
items.description: A 1923 swimming grotto carved from a coral-rock quarry, fed by spring water, with caves, waterfalls and Venetian bridges. A one-of-a-kind, storybook swim for the whole family on a hot afternoon.

items.name: Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden
items.description: 83 acres of palms, cycads, flowering trees and a butterfly conservatory, with a tram if walking is tiring. Serene and shaded, a gentle morning for elders and a wonder for children, especially during the seasonal art and orchid shows.

items.name: Miracle Mile & downtown Coral Gables
items.description: A leafy, Mediterranean-styled main street of boutiques, galleries and fine restaurants, with fountains and canopy trees. A civilised, low-key afternoon of strolling and shopping away from the beach crowds.

items.name: Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park & Lighthouse
credentials: Cape Florida Light, U.S. National Register of Historic Places
items.description: The tip of Key Biscayne, with the 1825 Cape Florida Light, the oldest standing structure in Miami-Dade, and a calm, palm-backed beach 15 minutes from downtown. Climb the 109 steps for views over Stiltsville and the skyline; two Cuban-food cafes on site make an easy family day.

items.name: Crandon Park Beach
items.description: A two-mile crescent of soft sand with shallow, gentle water and cabanas, one of the calmest, most family-friendly beaches near the city. Quieter than South Beach; good for grandparents and small children who want the sea without the scene.

items.name: South Beach (Lummus Park beachfront)
items.description: The iconic wide white-sand beach backed by pastel lifeguard stands and the Art Deco skyline. Rent a private cabana for shade and service; the promenade behind is perfect for an evening stroll with the family.

items.name: Bal Harbour Beach & boardwalk
items.description: A refined, low-rise stretch of sand fronting the luxury enclave, linked by a shaded oceanfront boardwalk toward Surfside. Calm and discreet, the beach of choice if you want quiet luxury over spectacle.

items.name: Sunny Isles Beach
items.description: A broad, uncrowded beach lined with gleaming towers, favoured by international families for space and its easy villa-and-condo stays. Wide sand, warm water and a relaxed pace for a multi-day base.

items.name: Bal Harbour Shops
items.description: The most exclusive open-air mall in America, Chanel, Dior, Prada, Cartier and an expanded Tiffany among koi ponds and tropical greenery, anchored by Neiman Marcus and Saks. A major 2026 expansion is nearly doubling its size; peerless, unhurried luxury shopping with valet and fine dining.

items.name: Aventura Mall
items.description: The largest mall in South Florida, 300-plus stores balancing Hermès, Gucci and Louis Vuitton with everyday favourites and Nordstrom and Bloomingdale's anchors. Fully covered and cool, with a play area and slide tower for children; the practical choice for big family shopping.

items.name: Star Island celebrity-homes boat cruise
items.description: A 90-minute sightseeing cruise from Bayside past the waterfront mansions of Star, Palm and Hibiscus Islands and the downtown skyline. Charter a private yacht instead for a bespoke sunset run, the classic way to see Miami's wealth from the water.

items.name: Bayside Marketplace & Bayfront Park
items.description: A waterfront marketplace of shops, cafes and live music beside the marina where most bay cruises depart, next to the green sweep of Bayfront Park. An easy, walkable staging point before a boat tour, with the skyline as backdrop.

items.name: Coconut Grove village & waterfront
items.description: Miami's oldest neighbourhood, leafy, bohemian and bayfront, with sidewalk cafes, sailing marinas and the CocoWalk arcade. A gentle, tree-shaded afternoon; pair it with Vizcaya just up the road.

items.name: Brickell & Brickell City Centre
items.description: Miami's glossy financial district, with a climate-controlled open-air shopping and dining complex, rooftop bars and river-mouth views. Sleek and cosmopolitan, good for an evening of dining and skyline drinks.

items.name: Little Haiti Cultural Complex
items.description: A Caribbean-styled arts centre with a gallery, dance and a marketplace, hosting Konpa concerts and guided neighbourhood tours through the culture and food of Haitian Miami. An off-the-beaten-path cultural afternoon most visitors miss.

items.name: Everglades day-trip: Shark Valley
credentials: Everglades National Park, UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.description: The northern gateway to the Everglades, where a 15-mile paved loop, by tram, bike or foot, puts alligators and wading birds within arm's reach, ending at a lookout tower over the sawgrass. A genuine wilderness half-day, naturalist-guided and gentle enough for all ages.

items.name: Everglades airboat safari
items.description: A fast, exhilarating glide across the wetlands with a wildlife show and gators up close, at parks along the Tamiami Trail west of the city. Book a private boat for a calmer, unhurried run; a thrill the grandchildren will talk about for years.

items.name: Key West & the Florida Keys day-trip
items.description: A scenic drive down the Overseas Highway across turquoise water to Florida's southernmost city, Duval Street, Hemingway's house, Mallory Square sunsets and reef snorkelling. Long but rewarding; consider a chauffeur or a stay overnight to do it at leisure.

items.name: Islamorada & the Upper Keys
items.description: The gentler, closer Keys escape, sport-fishing capital, sandbar picnics, tarpon feeding and waterfront seafood, an hour and a half south. A relaxed alternative to the full Key West haul, easy as a private half-day charter.

items.name: Lincoln Road Mall
items.description: A pedestrian promenade of shops, cafes and galleries designed by Morris Lapidus, lined with fountains and shaded seating a block from the beach. An easy, car-free evening stroll for browsing and people-watching.

items.name: Faena District & the Faena Forum
items.description: A theatrical enclave of Alan Faena's making, a gilded Damien Hirst mammoth, a Rem Koolhaas-designed cultural forum and a hotel dripping in Baz Luhrmann drama. Come for a drink and the spectacle even if you stay elsewhere; unabashed, cinematic luxury.

items.name: Holocaust Memorial of Miami Beach
items.description: Kenneth Treister's powerful sculptural memorial, a giant bronze hand rising amid figures, set in a contemplative garden. A quiet, moving stop of real gravity a short walk from the Convention Center and Botanical Garden.

items.name: Miami Beach Botanical Garden
items.description: A serene 2.6-acre green pocket of palms, orchids, a Japanese garden and lily ponds in the middle of the city, and free to enter. A cool, shaded pause between the beach and the Convention Center.

items.name: The Wolfsonian–FIU
items.description: A design-and-decorative-arts museum in a striking 1927 building, exploring how design shaped the modern age, propaganda, industry, Art Deco objects. A thoughtful, air-conditioned hour for design-minded visitors on Washington Avenue.

items.name: Zoo Miami
items.description: A vast cage-free, walk-and-tram safari park with Asian and African habitats and a Florida section, one of the country's largest zoos. A full, gentle family day; go early to beat the heat, and use the tram to spare tired legs.

items.name: Deering Estate
credentials: U.S. National Register of Historic Places
items.description: Charles Deering's bayfront estate, historic houses, a fossil-rich hammock, mangrove shoreline and canoe access, quieter than its famous sibling Vizcaya. A tranquil nature-and-history morning for those who like their culture uncrowded.

items.name: Matheson Hammock Park & atoll pool
items.description: A man-made tidal atoll pool ringed by sand and palms beside Biscayne Bay, calm and shallow with the skyline in the distance. One of the safest, prettiest swims for small children, with a marina and cafe alongside.

items.name: Española Way
items.description: A pretty pedestrian lane of Mediterranean-revival buildings, string lights, tapas terraces and buskers a block off Ocean Drive. A charming spot for an early-evening aperitivo before dinner.

items.name: Pérez-area sunset sail / private yacht charter
items.description: Beyond the group cruises, Biscayne Bay is made for a private catamaran or motor-yacht charter, a captain, a chef, veg-friendly catering and a swim stop off a sandbar. The most memorable evening on the water, tailored entirely to your family.

items.name: Nightlife on Washington Avenue & the rooftops
items.description: Miami's after-dark reputation is earned, from South Beach clubs to rooftop lounges over Brickell and the Design District's sleeker bars. For UHNI guests, a host or table-service arrangement smooths the night; the concierge can curate a discreet, easy evening.

items.name: L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon
items.description: The Robuchon counter in the Design District, the only two-star table in Florida, for a third year running.

items.name: The Surf Club Restaurant
items.description: Thomas Keller's continental grand room inside the Four Seasons Surf Club, old-glamour Miami at its most refined.

items.name: Cote Miami
items.description: The Michelin-starred Korean steakhouse from New York, smokeless grills, dry-aged beef and endless Champagne.

items.name: Elcielo Miami
items.description: Juan Manuel Barrientos's multisensory Colombian tasting menu, theatre, memory and Andean flavour in Brickell.

items.name: Shingo
items.description: Shingo Akikuni's fourteen-seat omakase in the Gables, pristine edomae sushi of great precision.

items.name: Hiden
items.description: An eight-seat omakase behind a hidden door in Wynwood, Seijun Okano's singular, secret counter.

items.name: Ogawa
items.description: Refined Edomae-style omakase paired with rare Japanese whiskies, quiet mastery north of the city centre.

items.name: Tambourine Room by Tristan Brandt
items.description: Tristan Brandt's French cooking with Asian notes inside the Carillon, a jewel-box tasting-menu room.

items.name: Ariete
items.description: Michael Beltran's New-American-meets-Cuban cooking in the Grove, personal, Miami-rooted and quietly excellent.

items.name: Boia De
items.description: A tiny, cult Italian-American counter in a strip mall, outsized cooking, no ceremony, a real find.

items.name: Le Jardinier Miami
items.description: Alain Verzeroli's garden-driven French room in the Design District, seasonal, light and beautifully composed.

items.name: Los Félix
items.description: Masa-driven modern Mexican in the Grove, a Green Star kitchen built on heirloom corn and local produce.

items.name: Stubborn Seed
items.description: Top Chef winner Jeremy Ford's refined, ingredient-led room, a Green Star for its sustainable kitchen.

items.name: EntreNos
items.description: A twelve-seat counter from Evan Burgess and Osmel Gonzalez, hyper-local, sustainable, deeply personal.

items.name: Mutra
items.description: The world's first kosher restaurant to earn a Michelin star, Raz Shabtai's inventive seasonal Middle Eastern.

items.name: Ghee Indian Kitchen
items.description: Chef Niven Patel's farm-driven Indian cooking, coastal curries and roasted vegetables from his own fields.

items.name: Phuc Yea
items.description: Vietnamese-Cajun cooking with real swagger, a beloved, boldly flavoured MiMo institution.

items.name: Lucali
items.description: The Brooklyn pizza legend's Miami outpost, thin-crust pies made one at a time, worth the wait.

items.name: Sanguich de Miami
items.description: The definitive Cuban sandwich, made from scratch, house-cured meats and pressed medianoche on Calle Ocho.

items.name: Broken Shaker
credentials: World's 50 Best Bars (multiple years; first Miami bar to make the list)
Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Award, Best American High Volume Cocktail Bar
items.description: The garden bar that put Miami on the world cocktail map, herb-driven, barefoot-glamour drinking by the pool.

items.name: The Living Room, Faena Hotel
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Two-Key, Forbes 5-Star hotel, a Miami Beach landmark
items.description: A drink amid Faena's gilded, red-velvet theatre, the most glamorous hotel bar in Miami Beach.

items.name: The Bar at The Surf Club
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Two-Key, Forbes 5-Star hotel (Four Seasons Surf Club)
items.description: A jewel-box bar in a restored 1930s beach club, Winston Churchill drank here; the glamour is real.

items.name: Café La Trova
items.description: Julio Cabrera's Havana-style cantina, the finest Cuban cocktails in America, poured by master cantineros.

items.name: ViceVersa
items.description: A refined, ingredient-driven cocktail room that broke into the region's very best, Miami's newest star bar.

items.name: Sweet Liberty Drinks & Supply Co.
credentials: Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Award, Best American Cocktail Bar (Best New, 2016)
items.description: John Lermayer's warm, all-day neighbourhood bar, serious cocktails without a shred of pretension.

items.name: Sugar, EAST Miami
credentials: Widely rated among Miami's best rooftop bars
items.description: A Balinese-styled rooftop garden on the 40th floor, the highest bar in the city, with 360° bay-and-skyline views.

plan.heading: 3 days in Miami, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Settle into a cabana suite at The Setai, then a slow walk through the Art Deco district off Ocean Drive before the crowds gather.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A private charter out of Miami Beach Marina to sandbars and a quiet swim, back for a late afternoon on the sand.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Carbone Miami in the Design District, then a nightcap at Sweet Liberty.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Institute of Contemporary Art and the Design District's flagship maisons before lunch at MC Kitchen.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Rubell Museum and Wynwood's serious galleries and studios, at your own pace.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Omakase at Ogawa, then Espanola Way for a quiet drink.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The gardens and villa at Vizcaya Museum before the heat, with time along Biscayne Bay.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Coconut Grove and a table at Cote or a long lunch at the Biltmore in Coral Gables.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sunset dinner at Stubborn Seed in South Beach to close.

items.name: South Beach
items.description: Art Deco, ocean and nightlife, iconic but busy; ideal for a couple of nights, less so for a whole stay.

items.name: Design District / Midtown
items.description: Galleries, flagship boutiques and the best new restaurants, the tasteful, walkable base on the mainland.

items.name: Coconut Grove
items.description: Leafy, low-rise and family-old-money; bayfront calm for travellers who want green over glitz.

events.name: Art Basel Miami Beach
events.note: The city's marquee week; the fair anchors dozens of satellite shows and the design world descends.

events.name: Ultra Music Festival
events.note: Electronic-music weekend at Bayfront Park that headlines Miami Music Week.

events.name: Miami International Boat Show
events.note: One of the world's largest boat shows, a fixture of the city's on-water calendar over Presidents' Day weekend.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in Bal Harbour or the South-of-Fifth end of South Beach for quiet and space away from the party strip; dress is relaxed but polished, and reserve beachfront restaurants well ahead in season (December–April).

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Arrive into Miami International (MIA), roughly 20 minutes from the coast; a chauffeured car meets you planeside where arranged, or a private car from arrivals to Miami Beach, Bal Harbour or Brickell.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car and driver is the way to move between the beach, the Design District and Coconut Grove; distances are short but the heat and valet-only culture make walking impractical.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: US eSIMs (Airalo, T-Mobile) activate instantly and coverage is universal; every good hotel and restaurant has fast wifi.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: US dollars; cards are used for everything and contactless is standard; tip 18–20 percent in restaurants and a few dollars for valet and bellhops.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: December to April is dry, warm and clear, the reason to come; June to October is hot, humid and inside Atlantic hurricane season, with September and October the wettest and riskiest.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No direct service from India; the clean routing is one stop through the Gulf, Qatar (Doha) or Emirates (Dubai), at roughly 19-22 hours door to door, both strong in business and first. Doha's Al Mourjan and Dubai's Emirates lounge make the layover restful; European hubs (BA via London, Lufthansa via Frankfurt) work but add time.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required beyond routine; tap water is safe. Safe for the traveller staying in Brickell, South Beach, Coral Gables or Bal Harbour; ordinary big-city caution at night. Sun and heat are the real hazards in summer.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian dining is effortless, the city runs on it, and Jain-friendly meals are readily adapted. Strong Indian options in and around the metro; the sizeable Gujarati and South Indian community means authentic thalis and dosas are close at hand.
